novelty.justification: The claim hypothesizes that numerals occupy a "shared, language-independent magnitude subspace" and, more distinctively, that "arithmetic operates over this shared code before language-specific verbalization," so its novelty route is a cross-lingual mechanism connecting representation to computation rather than merely a new language setting. Searches around “multilingual LLM shared numeral magnitude representation,” “cross-lingual number-word arithmetic circuits,” and “language-independent numerical manifold activation patching” identify the closest precedents as Wendler et al., "Separating Tongue from Thought" (2024), which causally studies language-agnostic concepts, and Engels et al., "Language Models Represent Numbers on a Helix" (2024), which characterizes numerical geometry and arithmetic-related interventions, while neither establishes a shared multilingual numeral code consumed by arithmetic before language-specific output. Combining those lines is a substantive natural extension rather than a wholly new interpretability paradigm: the specific computation-over-cross-lingual-code relationship appears new and requires non-trivial integration, but is reasonably predictable from existing language-agnostic concept and numerical-manifold findings.
